NOTE_PURPOSE: Bring-up constraint set. Every key is identical to config.json except CLOCK_PERIOD and the three SDC keys: the period here is 32.0 ns, a figure taken from measurement and not from the specification. The run at the 30.0 ns gate, RUN_2026-11-09_21-14-43, closed eight of the nine corners and missed the ninth by 0.4906 ns in max_ss_100C_1v60 over 35 register to register paths, so that layout needed 30.49 ns in the slow corner by first order. 32.0 ns leaves just under 1.5 ns against the rerouting a different period causes, which is visible in the history: the same RTL routed at the 8.0 ns gate measured -15.7205 ns in that corner, a first-order 23.7 ns, and routed again at 30.0 ns it measured -0.4906 ns, a first-order 30.5 ns, so each rerun moves the design by more than a tenth of a nanosecond. The declared 250 MHz budget stays in config.json, in lingologos.sdc and in the datasheet, where it is marked NOT MEASURED.
NOTE_HOW_TO_SELECT: asic_chip/scripts/build_gds.sh uses this file unless LL_OPENLANE_CONFIG is set to config.json. See asic_chip/doc/build_instructions.md.
NOTE_OPENLANE_VERSION: Keys are OpenLane 1 flow.tcl names, which OpenLane 2 keeps in its Classic flow. That mapping has run three times on 2026-11-09 with openlane 2.3.10 in a container. The last run, RUN_2026-11-09_21-14-43, went through all 78 steps of the Classic flow in 12 min 12 s, wrote three GDSII files, and printed Antenna Passed, LVS Passed and DRC Passed in Misc.ReportManufacturability; it then exited non zero on deferred setup violations in one corner and hold violations in seven. QUIT_ON_TIMING_VIOLATIONS and RUN_CVC are not keys of OpenLane 2.3.10 and were removed from this file when the flow reported them as unknown or removed, and QUIT_ON_LINTER_ERRORS is now spelled ERROR_ON_LINTER_ERRORS. PNR_SDC_FILE and SIGNOFF_SDC_FILE name the same constraint file as SDC, which is what keeps the place and route steps off the generic fallback SDC. See doc/build_instructions.md and doc/verification_report.md.
NOTE_TIMING: Measured on RUN_2026-11-09_21-14-43, the 30.0 ns gate: setup worst slack -0.4906 ns in max_ss_100C_1v60, total negative slack -13.5139 ns over 35 violating paths, every one of them register to register, starting at _17334_/Q over the net core_pc[2]. The other eight corners were positive at that period, +1.1885 min_ss, +0.3841 nom_ss, +14.4003/+14.9556/+15.4798 in the three tt corners and +20.1103/+20.5284/+20.8555 in the three ff corners, so the period this design needs is set by max_ss alone. Hold was still negative in seven corners, worst -0.1540 ns in max_ss_100C_1v60 with total negative slack -0.9162 ns over 10 violating paths, and every one of those paths is spelled [hold in-reg] in the violator list, an input port to a register; the two ff corners with the mildest numbers had 1 path at -0.0024 ns and 0 paths. The mechanism is measured, not assumed: the metrics of OpenROAD.STAMidPNR right after OpenROAD.ResizerTimingPostGRT report worst hold slack +0.1002 ns with zero violations in nom_tt_025C_1v80 on global-route parasitics, while the same corner at signoff on the extracted SPEF of OpenROAD.RCX reports -0.0585 ns. Detailed routing plus extraction therefore costs those paths about 0.16 ns, and the Classic flow has no resizer after OpenROAD.DetailedRouting, so nothing repairs that gap. PL_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN and GRT_RESIZER_HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN, whose installed defaults are 0.10 and 0.05 ns, are set to 0.40 ns here so the resizer overfixes hold past zero instead of stopping at it. The 0.30 ns minimum external input delay in the SDC is still well below the 2.18 ns of clock insertion delay that run measured in the slow corner, which is what makes those input paths expensive to hold; if the overfix does not close them, the honest next step is to widen the declared input delay window in the SDC, not to relax the checker. OpenLane 2 fails a flow only on corners matched by SETUP_VIOLATION_CORNERS and HOLD_VIOLATION_CORNERS, and the sky130 compatibility layer sets that to the pattern *tt*, so both keys are set to all nine corners here and a green run will mean all nine closed.
NOTE_ANTENNA: Answered by RUN_2026-11-09_21-14-43. The previous run, at the 8.0 ns gate, ended with 54 antenna pin violations on 46 nets, worst ratio 5.20, and only 468 diode cells inserted, because DIODE_INSERTION_STRATEGY had silently switched RUN_HEURISTIC_DIODE_INSERTION and DIODE_ON_PORTS off. With those keys set directly, the antenna report OpenROAD.CheckAntennas writes after OpenROAD.DetailedRouting is an empty table and Misc.ReportManufacturability prints Antenna Passed. The price is measured and worth knowing: the metrics of OpenROAD.FillInsertion count 16898 instances of class antenna_cell, the die went from 350447 to 393012 square micrometres and the standard cell area from 169306 to 204806 square micrometres, and detailed route settled at 660126 micrometres of wire over 134302 vias in eight iterations with zero design rule errors. HEURISTIC_ANTENNA_THRESHOLD 60 is an aggressive threshold; if the area matters, raising it toward 90 is the knob that trades antenna margin for area, and the run then has to be checked again. DIODE_INSERTION_STRATEGY stays absent on purpose: OpenLane 2 accepts the OpenLane 1 number and then overwrites RUN_HEURISTIC_DIODE_INSERTION and DIODE_ON_PORTS from it, whatever this file said.
NOTE_PATHS: A dir:: token resolves to the directory holding this config file, so the RTL sources are referenced one level up, in asic_chip/rtl. tests/test_asic_compiler.py expands every dir:: entry and fails if the named file is missing, which keeps this list honest without running the flow.
NOTE_ROM: The instruction memory is a 128 by 32 bit read only array initialized in an initial block. Yosys realizes it as constant logic in this flow; production would replace it with a hard ROM macro.
NOTE_DEBUG_PORTS: LL_DEBUG_PORTS is deliberately undefined here, so the dbg_ port group does not exist in the synthesized netlist and no package pin is reserved for it.
